verdicts.quote: "You can use OAuth 2 to authenticate all your application's API requests to Zendesk."
verdicts.reason: Zendesk directs developers to use OAuth 2.0 as the standard API auth method (and is deprecating API tokens), so OAuth2 is the primary auth.

verdicts.quote: "You must request a global OAuth client from Zendesk to create global OAuth tokens."
verdicts.reason: For multi-tenant/public distribution you need a Zendesk-approved global OAuth client (review), matching “app_review.” Single-account OAuth clients are self-serve in Admin Center.

verdicts.quote: "You'll find APIs for ticketing, help center, live chat, voice, sales CRM as well as... omnichannel routing and custom data."
verdicts.reason: The official reference spans many products and resources, indicating broad API coverage.

verdicts.quote: "When you connect Zendesk to an MCP server, the MCP client finds all of the tools the MCP server has..."
verdicts.reason: Zendesk publishes and maintains an official MCP client (GA). Zendesk also documents its own MCP server via Bridge/EAP, confirming an official MCP offering.

verdicts.quote: "When Zendesk approves your global OAuth client, Zendesk may configure allowed scopes on the client..."
verdicts.reason: Building is feasible today (self-serve OAuth per account; comprehensive APIs), but production multi-tenant apps require Marketplace/global OAuth approval, so “ready_with_caveats.”
